clinicalPearls: Theca-lutein cysts are the largest of the functional ovarian cysts and are characteristically bilateral and multilocular, arising from excessive or prolonged stimulation of ovarian theca cells by human chorionic gonadotrophin.

They are the classic ovarian finding of gestational trophoblastic disease (complete hydatidiform mole and choriocarcinoma) and also accompany multiple gestation, fetal hydrops, ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome, and exogenous gonadotrophin or clomifene therapy.
On ultrasound the enlarged ovaries show numerous thin-walled locules in a 'spoke-wheel' pattern, usually without solid components.
Most are asymptomatic and found incidentally, but large cysts may cause pelvic pressure, and complications include torsion, rupture, intraperitoneal haemorrhage and occasionally ascites.

Because they are hCG-dependent, they regress once the stimulus is removed (after evacuation of a mole, delivery, or resolution of the underlying cause), although regression may lag behind the fall in hCG by weeks to months.
Management is conservative and expectant; surgery is reserved for acute complications such as torsion or haemorrhage, ideally with ovarian conservation.
In gestational trophoblastic disease, persistent or re-enlarging theca-lutein cysts should prompt reassessment for persistent trophoblastic activity.
Maternal virilisation and clinical hyperthyroidism (from the weak thyrotrophic activity of hCG) are occasionally seen when hCG concentrations are very high.
reference.pathophysiology: Theca-lutein cysts develop when ovarian theca-interna cells are excessively stimulated by human chorionic gonadotrophin, which acts on the luteinising-hormone receptor to drive luteinisation, follicular over-recruitment and cystic dilatation. Markedly raised hCG, as in complete molar pregnancy, choriocarcinoma or multiple gestation, is the usual driver, although heightened ovarian sensitivity can produce them at more modest levels. The affected ovaries enlarge and become studded with multiple thin-walled, fluid-filled cysts lined by luteinised theca and granulosa cells, frequently bilateral and symmetrical. The luteinised cells may secrete androgens, and the high hCG can exert weak thyroid-stimulating activity. Because the cysts are functional and hormone-dependent, removal or decline of the hCG source allows involution.
additionalDifferentials: Hyperreactio luteinalis (florid theca-lutein cysts in pregnancy without trophoblastic disease)
Bilateral cystic ovarian neoplasm (mucinous or serous cystadenoma, borderline tumour)
Bilateral haemorrhagic corpus luteum cysts or endometriomas
additionalInvestigations: Quantitative serum hCG and its trend
Pelvic ultrasound with Doppler to assess cyst morphology, ovarian perfusion and possible torsion
Uterine evaluation for hydatidiform mole or retained trophoblastic tissue
Thyroid function tests if clinically hyperthyroid
Serum androgens if virilisation is present
Chest imaging where choriocarcinoma or metastatic trophoblastic disease is suspected
redFlags: Acute severe pelvic pain with peritonism suggesting torsion, rupture or haemorrhage
Plateauing or rising hCG after molar evacuation indicating persistent gestational trophoblastic neoplasia
Solid or papillary components, or failure to regress, raising suspicion of neoplasm
reference.prognosis: The cysts are benign and self-limiting and almost always involute spontaneously once the hCG source resolves. The outlook is excellent provided complications such as torsion or haemorrhage are managed and any underlying trophoblastic disease is treated.
pitfalls: Resecting hormone-dependent cysts that would regress spontaneously, sacrificing ovarian tissue
Failing to investigate for gestational trophoblastic disease when bilateral theca-lutein cysts are found
Misinterpreting the multicystic ovaries as malignancy
Attributing all pelvic pain to the cysts and missing a coexisting torsion
Expecting immediate regression and re-intervening before the natural lag after hCG decline
references: Blaustein's Pathology of the Female Genital Tract
